selectionNotes: Two 2013 convex archive solutions remain. Archive model 570 pole (173,-78) differs from the nominal table pole (156,-76) in Hanuš et al. (2013); the alternate archive pole (306,-67) likewise differs from nominal (333,-73). The archived solution, not an exact paper-table attitude, owns this presentation. Fine structure and a preferred pole are not established.
sourceLimitations: The pinned mesh is an inverse model, not a directly sampled surface. No registered reflectance mosaic is supplied by this release; a neutral grid must mark unavailable imagery. Fine-scale craters, regolith and albedo are unresolved. Absolute rotational phase is illustrative. Two 2013 convex archive solutions remain. Archive model 570 pole (173,-78) differs from the nominal table pole (156,-76) in Hanuš et al. (2013); the alternate archive pole (306,-67) likewise differs from nominal (333,-73). The archived solution, not an exact paper-table attitude, owns this presentation. Fine structure and a preferred pole are not established.

calibration.uncertaintyKind: Formal catalog uncertainty; excludes extra shape, spin and thermal-model systematics. It is not the total uncertainty of the displayed physical scale.
calibration.additionalSystematics: Usui2011§2.3 explicitly omits unquantified shape/spin/thermal-model effects; rotation can add a few to about10%in size, especially for fewdetections. No invented numerical confidence interval is assigned to these unquantified effects.
calibration.diameterSemantics: Mean fitted diameter of a nonrotating sphere in the modified Standard Thermal Model. Its use as the volume-equivalent diameter of the separate convex DAMIT mesh is an explicit display-scale approximation, not a published physical-volume calibration.
calibration.limitations: The physical size is approximately calibrated by assigning the AKARI thermal effective diameter to the mesh volume-equivalent diameter. Neither source mesh nor spin is modified. Convex inversion supplies only broad outline; no resolved craters, concavities, reflectance or regolith texture can be inferred. Two 2013 convex archive solutions remain. Archive model 570 pole (173,-78) differs from the nominal table pole (156,-76) in Hanuš et al. (2013); the alternate archive pole (306,-67) likewise differs from nominal (333,-73). The archived solution, not an exact paper-table attitude, owns this presentation. Fine structure and a preferred pole are not established.
